title: My Honest Take on the Pear Tallow Balm for Spring Skin
body:
Okay so. My face feels like a balloon that’s been left in the sun for a week. You know that feeling? It’s spring, supposedly. The air is doing this thing where it’s warm one second and then it’s like a cold slap the next. My skin has no idea what to do. It’s not winter-dry anymore, but it’s not summer-oily. It’s just… confused. And tight. And it gets these random itchy patches near my jawline that make me look like I’m having a silent argument with myself. I was in the bathroom this morning, poking at it, and I was like, what even is the plan here. I need something that isn’t a heavy winter thing but isn’t that watery gel stuff that evaporates in five minutes. Anyway, that’s how I ended up putting beef fat on my face. This whipped tallow balm, the pear one. I know. It sounds like a weird cooking experiment. But my skin’s been so weird this spring, and I was desperate.

I tried a lot of stuff before this. There was that expensive blue bottle from the fancy store. Felt nice going on, did nothing. There was the drugstore lotion that smelled like a fake flower garden and just sat on top of my skin, all shiny. I even tried that “skin cycling” thing for like, three days. Too many steps. My routine now is basically: splash face with water that’s either too hot or too cold because my faucet is ancient, stare at my reflection for a minute, then put on this tallow stuff. That’s it. Sometimes I forget. But when I remember, my skin just… chills out. It stops feeling like it’s two sizes too small for my skull.

## Why I Even Tried Beef Tallow on My Face

Look, I get it. The word “tallow” makes you think of candles or old-timey cooking. Not skincare. I was scrolling on my phone one night, it was late, like 1 AM, and my cheek was so tight it almost hurt to smile. I saw this Etsy shop mentioned somewhere. Someone was raving about their tallow balm. My first thought was, absolutely not. My second thought was, well, my great-grandmother probably used something like this and her skin looked fine in pictures. My third thought was fueled by desperation and a late-night “add to cart” mentality. I got the pear scent because it sounded the least intimidating. Figured if I was gonna smear rendered beef fat on myself, it should at least smell vaguely fruity.

The jar showed up maybe a week later. It’s small. Unassuming. Made in France, which for some reason made me feel fancier about the whole beef fat situation. The texture is weird. Not bad weird. It’s solid in the jar but if you scoop a tiny bit with your finger, it melts immediately. Like, the heat from your skin just turns it into an oil. It doesn’t feel greasy, though. That’s the part that got me. It just… sinks in. Disappears. My skin drinks it. The science-y reason, which I looked up after because I was curious, is that it’s really close to the oils our own skin makes. So it’s not a foreign substance sitting on top, clogging things. It’s like it’s giving your skin back something it recognizes. Which, when you think about it, makes a lot more sense than putting ten synthetic chemicals on your face.

## What This Pear Tallow Balm Actually Does

So the smell. It’s pear. But not like a Jolly Rancher or a candle. It’s subtle. Like you cut up a real pear on a wooden cutting board and your hands smell like that afterwards. A clean, fresh, slightly sweet smell. It’s not strong. It’s just nice. It doesn’t linger all day, which I prefer. I hate when my face perfume fights with my actual perfume.

Here’s what it does for my spring skincare drama. The dry, tight feeling? Gone in maybe two minutes after I put it on. The random itchy patches? They just stopped appearing. I used to get this rough, sandpapery texture on my forehead every April. It’s smooth now. I don’t know how else to say it. It just made my skin feel normal again. Not “perfect,” not “filtered,” just… comfortable. Like it’s not throwing a tantrum about the barometric pressure changing every five minutes. I use it at night mostly. Sometimes in the morning if my skin feels extra parched. A little goes a really long way. This tiny jar has lasted me over two months and I’m maybe halfway through.

Oh, and I started putting it on my hands. My knuckles always crack in the spring when I’m gardening. I was planting some herbs last weekend—basil, I think, or maybe it was thyme—and my hands were a mess. Dirt under my nails, skin all dry. Washed them, put a dab of the tallow balm on, and by the next morning the cracks were just… healed. No joke. It’s like the ultimate dry spring skin cheat code.

## My Skin After a Few Weeks of This Stuff

I’m not a skincare blogger. I don’t take progress pictures. But I can tell you what I noticed. My foundation doesn’t look weird and flaky anymore. It just goes on smooth. I stopped carrying that little tube of emergency hand cream in my purse because I don’t need it. The skin around my nails looks less ragged. My elbows are smoother. I know, random. But it’s true.

The biggest thing is I just don’t think about my skin as much. It’s not a problem I’m constantly trying to solve. It’s just there, doing its thing, feeling fine. For someone whose face used to feel like a weathervane for every seasonal change, that’s a big deal. It’s one less thing to stress about. My routine is stupid simple: water, tallow balm, done. Sometimes sunscreen if I’m going out. That’s it. I have more time to be annoyed about other stuff, like why my neighbor always mows his lawn at 8 AM on a Saturday.

Would I buy it again? I already did. I got a second jar last week because I was getting low and I didn’t want to run out. I even got one for my mom. She has super sensitive skin and everything makes her red. She called me last week and was like, “What is this magic beef butter?” She loves it. I told her not to call it that.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, honestly. It sounds wild but it makes sense. Our skin knows what to do with it because it’s similar to our own natural oils. It’s not like putting motor oil on your face. It’s more like giving your skin a food it actually recognizes.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
I was worried about this too. My skin can get weird bumps if I use something heavy. But this doesn’t feel heavy. It melts and absorbs so fast. For me, it hasn’t clogged anything. If anything, my skin seems more balanced. Less likely to freak out and produce a bunch of extra oil.

**What does the pear tallow balm smell like?**
It’s a fresh, real pear smell. Not candy. Not overpowering. Just a light, clean sweetness that goes away pretty quickly. It’s nice. If you hate scented stuff, they probably have an unscented one.

Anyway. If your skin is being difficult this spring, doing that weird tight-flaky-confused dance, this might be worth a shot. I got mine from this little Etsy shop, The Tallow Pot. No one’s paying me to say this. I just found something that works when nothing else did. My skin’s happy, I’m happy, and I don’t have to think about it anymore. That’s all I wanted.
